note: Facts and sources behind the member descriptions in IL.json, gathered 2026-10-05. "review" holds research notes for a human check; "issues" lists open questions.

byways.name: Great River Road
byways.designation: National Scenic Byway and All-American Road
byways.where: Along the Mississippi down Illinois's western border, from Galena (East Dubuque area) to the Cairo area; about 550 miles in Illinois

facts.fact: The Illinois Great River Road is about 550 miles long and runs almost the full length of the state, in northern and southern sections.
Stops include Galena's downtown, the working Dutch windmill 'De Immigrant' at Fulton, Cahokia, and the Devil's Backbone rock formations at Grand Tower.
FHWA lists the Great River Road as both an All-American Road and a National Scenic Byway.
Galena is a river town full of historic buildings; the Illinois route also passes Nauvoo, Pere Marquette State Park and Cahokia Mounds State Historic Site.

byways.review: Official site is run by Great Rivers Country with IDOT grant funding; the Mississippi River Parkway Commission state page is https://experiencemississippiriver.com/states/illinois/.

byways.name: Meeting of the Great Rivers Scenic Route
byways.designation: National Scenic Byway (first designated an Illinois State Scenic Byway in 1998)
byways.where: IL 3, IL 143 and IL 100 from Hartford (New Poag Road) through Alton and Elsah to Pere Marquette State Park near Grafton; Madison and Jersey counties; 33 miles

facts.fact: The 33-mile byway begins in Hartford at IL 3 and New Poag Road, follows IL 3, 143 and 100, and ends at Pere Marquette State Park in Grafton.

Elsah, once a steamboat landing known for stone houses, was the first entire village placed on the National Register of Historic Places, in 1973; Lewis and Clark wintered at Camp River Dubois near Hartford.
The Piasa Bird, a legendary creature painted on the bluffs along the Mississippi, is at Alton on the byway.

Pere Marquette State Park, the north end, sits at the confluence of the Mississippi and Illinois rivers; the route was an Illinois State Scenic Byway on June 8, 1998 and a National Scenic Byway on June 15, 2000.

byways.review: IDOT GIS names it 'Meeting of the Great Rivers Road' and its segments sum to 56 miles, against the official 33. Overlaps the Great River Road.

byways.name: Historic Route 66
byways.designation: National Scenic Byway and All-American Road
byways.where: Old US 66 alignments from Chicago southwest through Joliet, Pontiac and Springfield to the Mississippi at the Chain of Rocks Bridge

facts.fact: Route 66 begins in Chicago; stops include the Gemini Giant at Wilmington and the Illinois Route 66 Hall of Fame and Museum at Pontiac.
In Springfield the route passes the Cozy Dog Drive-In and the Route 66 Drive-In Theater, and it ends at the Mississippi near the Old Chain of Rocks Bridge.
FHWA lists Historic Route 66 as both an All-American Road and a National Scenic Byway.

byways.review: Official site is the Illinois Route 66 Scenic Byway organization.

byways.name: Illinois River Road
byways.where: Both banks of the Illinois River from Ottawa through Peoria to Havana, about 150 miles of corridor (291 miles including loops); ten counties

facts.fact: The byway runs about 150 miles along the Illinois River from Ottawa south to Havana, through a ten-county region with some 100 natural and historic sites.
Starved Rock State Park on the byway has 13 miles of trails through 18 glacier-carved canyons and 14 waterfalls.
Peoria's 2.52-mile Grandview Drive was called the 'world's most beautiful drive' by Theodore Roosevelt on a 1910 visit.

byways.review: illinoisriverroad.org returns 403 to curl but loads in a browser (verified with WebFetch).

byways.name: Lincoln Highway
byways.where: US 30, IL 31 and IL 38 from the Indiana line through Frankfort, Joliet, Aurora, Geneva, DeKalb, Rochelle and Dixon to Fulton on the Mississippi; 179 miles

facts.fact: The 179-mile Illinois route follows US 30 for much of its way, then IL 31 north through the Fox River Valley and IL 38 west through DeKalb and Dixon.
Rochelle's old-time Standard Oil filling station is restored as a visitors center, and Fulton has a nine-story Dutch windmill with river views and a levee path.
Franklin Grove's restored 1860 general store houses the Lincoln Highway Association's national headquarters.

byways.review: The byway's own site listed by FHWA (drivelincolnhighway.com) no longer resolves; the Enjoy Illinois page is used instead. Catalog designation also lists 'Illinois State Scenic Byway', a 1990s state tier that no longer appears on any current state page.

byways.name: Ohio River Scenic Byway
byways.where: Around the southern tip of Illinois along the Ohio River, through the Shawnee National Forest and river towns from Shawneetown to Cairo and Thebes; 188 miles in Illinois

facts.fact: The Illinois section of the byway is 188 miles long, winding around the southern tip of the state through the Shawnee National Forest.
Cave-in-Rock State Park and the Garden of the Gods are attractions along the way, and Metropolis has a 15-foot Superman statue on its town square.
Mound City National Cemetery holds some 2,700 Union and Confederate graves.

byways.review: 'where' endpoints are approximate; the sources fetched do not give exact Illinois termini. The byway continues into Indiana and Ohio.

byways.name: Historic National Road
byways.where: US 40 (paralleling I-70) from Marshall through Greenup, Effingham and Vandalia to East St. Louis; 164 miles

facts.fact: The Illinois National Road runs 164 miles from Marshall to East St. Louis, mirrored by US 40 and I-70; it was the first federally funded road in U.S. history.
At Greenup the Jackson Truss covered timber bridge, completed in 2000, replaced an earlier bridge.
Vandalia was the state capital from 1819 to 1839, and Abraham Lincoln served in the legislature at its statehouse; a Madonna of the Trail statue stands on the grounds.

byways.review: FHWA lists it as an All-American Road only. The national organization site listed by FHWA (nationalroad.org) fails TLS; the Enjoy Illinois page is used instead.

issues: Illinois has no current state designation list: all seven roads are national byways. Wikipedia records the Meeting of the Great Rivers as an Illinois State Scenic Byway from June 8, 1998, and the catalog gives Lincoln Highway the same tag, but no current IDOT or tourism page mentions a state tier. If the chapter shows 'Illinois State Scenic Byway' anywhere, it should be described as historical.

IDOT's old scenic byways page (idot.illinois.gov/travel-information/tourism/scenic-byways.html) now redirects to the generic Travel and Maps page; the Enjoy Illinois page is the only current state listing.
drivelincolnhighway.com (Lincoln Highway byway site listed by FHWA) does not resolve; nationalroad.org fails TLS. Both roads use Enjoy Illinois pages as url.
IDOT GIS calls the Meeting of the Great Rivers 'Meeting of the Great Rivers Road' with 56 summed miles against the official 33; check the catalog line (33 mi) is the right one.
Catalog lists Lincoln Highway with mapped miles 177 and IL only, matching the 179-mile Illinois route; fine.
Historic Route 66 catalog entry lists states AZ,IL,NM,OK only, while FHWA lists IL, MO, OK, NM, AZ, CA; the catalog may be missing states (not an Illinois problem).
